He believed that his rivals may exploit him, if they found out about the true nature of their relationship. Only Daru was privileged to call Darth Malgus by his real name, ''Veradun'', and that too in private.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

Malgus's personality justified his reputation as a fierce frontline warrior. He believed that he was born to fight and the Sith Empire was the instrument through which he realized his purpose. To him, the cost of the war did not matter regardless of how high it could be.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

Malgus perceived the Force as a source of conflict. Upon questioning from his friend Daru, he pointed out that the Force has light side and dark side which supports his perception. The Jedi, in his opinion, understood the Force partially. He acknowledged that some of them were powerful in its use. However, he regarded the Jedi as fools.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

Malgus did not tolerate failure at any cost.<ref name="Deceived Book" /> After he killed Jedi Master Kao Cen Darach and learned of Satele Shan and her comrades' escape, he felt disgusted with his Sith Master, Darth Vindican, for not assuring a total victory. Although he struck the wounded Pureblood Sith Lord down, he nonetheless savored their last victory together, which was of utmost significance.<ref name="Return" /> After the defeat on Alderaan, Malgus fell in to uncontrollable rage for a while, fought two Jedi regardless of his injuries, and killed them in an act of revenge before leaving.<ref name="Lesson" />

As a confident individual, Malgus was brave and boldly entered the Jedi Temple for confrontation with the Jedi with only his friend Daru by his side.<ref name="Deceived Book" /> When the captured shuttle crashed through the Temple's main entrance and skidded along the walkway, Malgus held his position while the majority of the Jedi around him prepared to flee if necessary.<ref name="Deceived Trailer" /> When Jedi Master Ven Zallow remained stationary, Malgus acknowledged his lack of fear with a nod of respect. Malgus took joy in killing Republic soldiers, especially after a commando used heavy firepower against him during the Battle of Alderaan. When faced with a desire to slay someone, he was prepared to kill his own allies if no enemies remained just to satisfy his rage.<ref name="Deceived Book" /> In later years, Zallow has been recognized as Malgus's most notable kill.<ref name="Holonet" />

Regardless of his contempt for the Jedi, Malgus was a man of principles. He was not accustomed to comforts and never drank [[Wine/Legends|wine]]. He always kept his promises. Jedi Knight Aryn Leneer wanted to avenge the death of her Jedi Master Ven Zallow, with whom she shared a powerful bond. She learned about the relationship between Malgus and Daru and wanted to exploit it. She decided to kill Daru to give Malgus a taste of the pain she felt because of his actions. However, Aryn controlled her emotions and let Daru live after encountering her in a Spaceport. Malgus also reached there and defeated Aryn in combat. But he spared her life in exchange of her sparing the life of Daru and gave her the option to leave Coruscant. Aryn was impressed but confused. While Aryn was leaving Coruscant, Malgus kept his promise and did not take advantage of her situation.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

However, Malgus realized his worst fears and his experience with Aryn changed him for good. He realized that Daru was his weakness just like the Jedi. He could no longer afford this weakness. Therefore, he killed his only friend and freed himself from the shackles of emotions.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

On Korriban, Malgus saw a vision of the Galaxy in flames; the fall of a Galaxy-spanning government (the Republic).<ref name="Deceived Book" /> However, Malgus was also a critic of the policy matters of the Sith Empire.<ref name="Holonet" /> After the Treaty of Coruscant, he felt disgusted with the politics of the Sith Empire and felt that the Republic was not the only system that required cleansing. Malgus especially had disagreements with his Sith rival Lord Adraas on various matters and killed him.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

Malgus was a reliable military commander and preferred to lead military expeditions into the unexplored territories with the objective of increasing the influence of the Sith Empire as a whole.<ref name="Holonet" />

===Rejecting the Sith Empire===
Over the years and by the time of the Cold War, Malgus grew disillusioned with the state of the Sith Empire, believing there was too much infighting inside the Dark Council. He also grew tired of the Empire rejecting the use of aliens in order to boost their forces, despite increasing losses to their military and resources. After the Emperor's death, Malgus took matters into his own hands and decided to build his own Empire, open to all Sith who wished to follow their passions, rejecting whatever titles they had gained which Malgus believed to be worthless.<ref name="Battle of Ilum" />

[[File:Darth_Malgus_breaks_free.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Malgus breaks free of the Sith Empire.]]
Malgus demanded respect in his new position as the self-proclaimed emperor of the new Sith regime. The Sith Lord claimed that the Empire's antiquated ideals would cause the Sith to wither away and if they wanted to survive they needed to build a more tolerant network. Malgus was willing to destroy the Emperor's Fortress in order to wipe out the fleets that were attacking them, believing that the fortress was a monument to the old Empire and its sacrifice was inevitable. The Sith Lord was willing to die for his cause, saying that even if he was defeated, the Empire would be reborn.<ref name="False Emperor" />

After his return during the Invasion of Ossus, Malgus seemingly became loyal to the Sith Empire once again,<ref name="Jedi Under Siege" /> but in reality he was just pretending to be while secretly collecting various Jedi and Sith artifacts behind the scenes.<ref name="Secrets of the Enclave" /> He also followed the trail of [[Darth Nul]], an ancient Sith Lord whose records were apparently deleted by the Empire.<ref name="Darth Nul" />

During his mission to Elom, Malgus talked to padawan Sa'har Kateen about how both Sith and Jedi maintained control over the galaxy by keeping to themselves the secrets of the force, not revealing it to those who they deem unworthy.<ref name="Disorder" /> After he was captured and imprisoned, Malgus recalled his vision of a galaxy in flames and claimed that he began something that would not end with him.<ref name="Ruins of Nul" />

==Powers and abilities==
===Lightsaber training===
[[File:Malgus-Return.jpg|thumb|250px|Darth Malgus's rare usage of two lightsabers.]]
Darth Malgus was an exceptionally talented duelist and specialized in using [[Force Enrage|rage]] and [[Form V/Legends|brute strength]] to defeat his opponents. Aside from his overwhelming physical strength, which served him well not only in lightsaber duels but also in [[Unarmed combat/Legends|hand-to-hand combat]], Malgus also often performed [[Form IV/Legends|acrobatics]] to increase his effectiveness in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. His speed was such that a normal human found it difficult to watch his movements in his duels.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

A ferocious Sith Warrior with a terrifying reputation,<ref name="Holonet" /> Darth Malgus relished engaging in combat on the front line.<ref name="Hope" /> He was personally responsible for the deaths of several highly skilled Jedi Masters. Malgus had shown to employ Jar'Kai in various situations, such as during the retaking of Korriban where he employed this style to kill the Jedi Battlemaster Kao Cen Darach despite the latter's proficiency in the same fighting style and victory over Malgus's Master, Darth Vindican. Malgus's strength, rage, and clear focus gave him an advantage and allowed him to swiftly [[Sun djem/Legends|deprive]] Kao of one of his lightsabers and finally slay the Jedi Master.<ref name="Return" /> Years later, during the Sacking of Coruscant, Malgus managed to impale Jedi Master Ven Zallow in a short but ferocious duel.<ref name="Deceived Trailer" /> Zallow was often regarded as his most famous kill.<ref name="Holonet" /> Another brief example of this was shown during his fight against Jedi Padawan Sa'har Kateen, where Malgus used Jar'Kai after taking Denolm Orr's lightsaber. Even as he got older, Malgus still remained a fierce duelist that managed to fight against both Masters and Padawans.<ref name="Disorder" />

===Force abilities===
{{Quote|Your instructors tell me that they've seen few with your potential in the Force.|Veradun's adoptive father|<ref name="Lesson" />}}
[[File:DarthMalgusLightning-Deceived.png|thumb|left|250px|Malgus unleashes Force lightning during the Sacking of Coruscant.]]
Darth Malgus utilized a variety of Force [[Force power/Legends|powers]] during the Sacking of Coruscant to defeat many Jedi and Republic soldiers who stood in his path, including saber throw, Force push, choke, jump, speed and lightning. Malgus used his emotions &mdash; such as anger and distaste of others &mdash; to fuel his power of the dark side. Malgus demonstrated the skill and power to handle multiple opponents simultaneously without much effort.<ref name="Deceived Trailer" />

In one instance, Malgus unleashed a powerful blast of Force lightning and killed 3 Jedi with it. Malgus himself could tolerate Force lightning attacks. During his duel with Lord Adraas, Malgus strode through the barrage of the Force lightning from his opponent using his lightsaber and fingers as conduit, and redirected it back towards his opponent to knock him off his feet.<ref name="Deceived Book" /> He perfected his application of Force lightning to a degree from which he could unleash a [[Force Maelstrom]].<ref name="Book of Sith" /> During the Battle of Ilum, he demonstrated an application of tutaminis when fired at by either the [[Voidhound]], [[Meteor (Havoc Squad)|Meteor]], [[Hunter (individual)|Hunter]] or [[Cipher Nine]], absorbing the [[Blaster/Legends|blasterfire]] with one hand.<ref name="False Emperor" />

Malgus also performed Force screams to make his hatred apparent to his opponents as well as destroy enemy fighters within his range.<ref name="Deceived Book" /><ref name="Book of Sith" /> During his raid of the Jedi Temple, Malgus unleashed power with an expression of his rage which shattered a nearby column of wall and send a rain of stone shards through the room when his friend Eleena Daru was struck down by his most powerful opponent in the region; Zallow.<ref name="Deceived Book" /><ref name="Deceived Trailer" /> Malgus used this ability once again during his raid of the resting place of Adraas, making his extreme hatred for him clearly visible by leaving a trail of destruction around him with it during his advance towards his powerful Sith rival.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

Malgus often used Force speed to augment his physical movements.<ref name="Return" /> When Malgus engaged Jedi Knight Aryn Leener in a duel, an observer attempted to watch them but could not properly see their movements because of their immense speed. Later on, Malgus used this ability once again while he was rushing towards the hangar in a [[Spaceport/Legends|Spaceport]] to rescue Daru from a threat, leaving the troops accompanying him far behind.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

[[File:Malgus_using_Force_maelstrom_BoS.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Malgus using Force Maelstrom to destroy his enemies.]]
Being strong in the Force, Malgus was proficient in the applications of [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]]. Malgus could counter-push his opponents in the mid-air while they would jump towards him to knock them out in the process.<ref name="Deceived Trailer" /> During the duel with Aryn, Malgus demonstrated the ability to hurl objects as missiles towards his opponent.<ref name="Deceived Book" /> Malgus could also perform Force grip and Force crush.<ref name="Deceived Book" /><ref name="Deceived Trailer" />

On Alderaan, a Zabrak Jedi used the Force to collapse two buildings on Malgus in an attempt to kill him. Malgus stood under the mountain of rubble composed of building parts made of duracrete and steel preventing it from crushing him beneath with the Force. Malgus controlled his anger and sharpened his power. He blew the rubble up and away from him, sending it crashing in adjacent buildings.<ref name="Lesson" />

Malgus also performed [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Wave|Force wave]] when he attempted to disperse a large crowd gathered outside a Medical Facility in Coruscant to check on Daru. The blast shoved everything away from him in all directions, and bodies slammed in to each other, walls, and windows. The nearby Transport lurched, and all the doors of the Medical Facility broke loose and fell to the ground.<ref name="Deceived Book" />

On Alderaan, Malgus also faced Jedi Master Satele Shan and her allies in single combat and tolerated heavy firepower and Force powers from his opponents which shattered large objects around him.<ref name="Hope" /> He was seriously injured but he survived and felt no pain.<ref name="Lesson" />

Malgus could also hide his presence in the Force.<ref name="Deceived Book" /> Interestingly, a Jedi on Alderaan used this ability to suppress his Force signature when he planned to ambush Malgus but it was not effective against him. Malgus still managed to sense his presence and foiled his plans.<ref name="Lesson" /> Malgus was so strong in the Force that it took various Force-users to immobilize him on Elom.<ref name="Ruins of Nul" />

==Equipment==
[[File:Malgus_Lightsaber.png|thumb|200px|Darth Malgus's lightsaber]]
Darth Malgus had a lightsaber with a black and silver colored metal hilt that emitted a red blade. The lightsabers' emitter section was flanked by two intimidating, blade-like pieces with an design cues taken from an axe.  By the time of the Third Galactic War, his lightsaber was damaged and battle-worn. After the Battle of Alderaan, Malgus donned a respirator mask<ref name="Deceived Book" /> that covered his nose, mouth, and neck.<ref name="Deceived Trailer" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|He's definitely not a hero, and he's not an anti-hero. My goal was to create a character that readers can respect but still abhor. I very much enjoy writing characters who live in a moral twilight.|Paul S. Kemp, on developing Malgus for ''The Old Republic: Deceived''|<ref name="Blaster (Star Wars Insider)">{{InsiderCite|123|Blaster}}</ref>}}
Darth Malgus first appeared as an unidentified Sith in the [[Deceived|''Deceived'' trailer]] to the upcoming video game, ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. In the trailer, Malgus &mdash; voiced by [[Jamie Glover]]<ref name="SWI113">{{InsiderCite|113|The Sacking of Coruscant}}</ref> &mdash; serves as narrator, though the character does have at least one line of dialogue, when he kills his Jedi opponent. Malgus was first identified in an [http://www.swtor.com/info/holonet/biographies/darth-malgus entry] on ''The Old Republic'' website's [[The Holonet|Holonet]] databank which features [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] phrases such as "Friend to [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]," "[[Yablari/Legends|Yablari]], [[Trandosha/Legends|Trandosha]], [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]]," and "First Contact." Malgus made appearances in the [[Hope (cinematic trailer)|''Hope'']] and [[Return (cinematic trailer)|''Return'' trailers]], and was featured as a major character in [[Paul S. Kemp]]'s novel ''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]'', released on [[March 22]], [[2011]]. Darth Malgus' armor was later released in-game as the "Sith Raider Armor", an armor set purchasable through the Cartel Market system.

The mission log text for "The Challenge of War" on Ilum refers to Malgus as a member of the Dark Council. However, the in-game dialogue does not refer to him as such, and it contradicts established details about Malgus's disinterest in serving on the Council.<ref name="Challenge">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|The Challenge of War|[[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]]}}</ref>

[[File:Darth_Malgus_Carbonite.jpg|thumb|200px|Concept art of Darth Malgus in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]]]
After his demise in the original game,<ref name="False Emperor" /> Darth Malgus was thought to be dead.<ref name="Annihilation" /> During San Diego Comic Con [[2015]] Cantina Tour, a fan-event hosted by [[BioWare]], a clip and several concept arts of a cut scene from the ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire]]'' cinematic trailer [[Sacrifice (cinematic trailer)|''Sacrifice'']] were showing him in [[carbonite]], brought by [[Thexan]] and [[Arcann]] before the [Emperor of the [[Eternal Empire]], Valkorion. However, besides being mentioned, Malgus never appeared in the extension, which was released later that year on [[October 27]].<ref name="SDCC 2015">{{WebCite|url=http://dulfy.net/2015/07/11/swtor-sdcc-story-panel-shows-fate-darth-malgus|text=SWTOR SDCC Story Panel shows the fate Darth Malgus|date=2015-07-11|work=dulfy.net|archivedate=20200502161022}}</ref> The character would later return in the course of the next expansion, ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne]]''.<ref name="Jedi Under Siege" />
